basis:
WHAT THIS FILE IS. The observed ENVELOPE of every entry the speed gate measures — the range it was actually seen over, with a tolerance, and never a single number pretending to be one. Recorded on the cell that reads it: ubuntu-latest, image ubuntu24/20260927.320, runner 2.337.0.

THREE WINDOWS, AND THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IN THIS FILE. The renderer workloads ship IDENTICAL code at all three commits — the rounds between them touched the workflow, the tests, the comparator and this document, never a renderer — so every post-split observation describes one program and all of them belong in one envelope:

    window 1  07:46-07:56Z  at 3c30eca  runs 36832215161 36832519319 36832824918 36833056763
    window 2  10:15-10:24Z  at 4c003c6  runs 36847969226 36848207890 36848474648 36848721383
    window 3  10:35-10:47Z  at 94e8a78  runs 36850024437 36850406095 36850650070 36850880222 36851111411

and they disagree by a factor of four on the same programs:

    entry                         window 1        window 2        window 3
    counter::unit-suite            16.593-23.203   22.852-24.544   21.657-24.360
    e2e::bench.render               0.056- 0.084     0.080- 0.087     0.079- 0.084
    e2e::bench.render-impact        1.019- 1.351     1.332- 1.404     1.045- 1.355
    e2e::bench.render-responsiveness 0.060- 0.080     0.078- 0.086     0.078- 0.082

THE SPREAD IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE WORKLOAD. It is the workload AND the state of the pool during the window: window 1 contains one clearly fast machine and several slow ones, windows 2 and 3 look like a quiet pool. So the renderer envelopes are the UNION of all thirteen observations per entry — 4 + 4 + 5 — because the busy window is the only evidence that a fast machine exists. An envelope built from a quiet window false-reds the first time the pool is busy, and a false red on main trains people to ignore the gate, which is the whole failure this change exists to remove. DO NOT SHRINK A TOLERANCE BECAUSE THE LAST RUNS WERE QUIET, and do not read a quiet window as the cell's characteristic spread.

Note the recorded maximum for render-impact is 1.414891, from window 1. An earlier draft of this file took its maximum from window 2 and recorded 1.403799 — under-recording the worst machine by exactly the mistake the rule above exists to prevent, in the same place it had already been made once in transcribed prose.

THE UNIT SUITE IS DIFFERENT, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT. Only windows 2 and 3 ran a tree whose suite matches this one's closely, and window 3's five runs are the ones that describe it: 21.657363-24.359847, a 12.5% spread. That is recorded — and it is NOT the tolerance. The same cell measured a suite of this scale at 39.8% in window 1, so 12.5% is what this workload looks like when the pool is quiet, not what it always looks like. A tolerance derived from it would false-red the next busy run on main. The tolerance stays 0.40, and 7.4%/12.5% are recorded as OBSERVED rather than as budgets.

WHY AN ENVELOPE AT ALL. CPU seconds exclude steal, so a co-tenant does not reach them — that is what makes them a magnitude where elapsed time is not. They are still hardware-dependent: a faster or narrower core runs the same instructions in fewer CPU seconds, and the pool spans instance types. A single stored value plus a budget wide enough to cover what the cell has shown would need a tolerance above 1.0 on some entries, which is not a loose gate but a gate that cannot fire.

WHY THE TOLERANCE IS THE OBSERVED SPREAD. The gate compares a per-run MINIMUM against a recorded MAXIMUM, so the machine's whole observed range is conceded for free and the tolerance only has to cover a head landing on a machine worse than any yet seen — one more spread-width. Per entry: unit suite 0.40 (the cell's demonstrated spread at this scale, not any single window's), bench.render 0.60, bench.render-impact 0.39, bench.render-responsiveness 0.45; a population takes its widest, so the renderer workloads carry 0.60.

WHAT THIS GATE THEREFORE CATCHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Nothing derived is written out here, because a transcribed ceiling was wrong twice in this file's history. The honest summary is uncomfortable: at these tolerances a DOUBLED workload is caught on the unit suite and on NONE of the three renderer workloads, because doubling the fastest machine observed lands under all three ceilings. The alternative — a tolerance tight enough to catch those doublings — is below the observed spread of every one of them, and would fire on ordinary pool variation. A gate that cries wolf is deader than one with a documented blind spot, so bench.render is NOT tuned and neither are its siblings. The gate catches a gross step change and the gross wall smoke bound; it will not catch a 20% regression anywhere. Read "load-invariant counter" as "a quantity the machine's load does not reach", not as "a sharp budget".

THE GROSS WALL SMOKE BOUND. `wall` is an envelope for the same reason, spanning the same three windows; at SMOKE_FACTOR 3.0 the ceilings are 168.5 seconds, 0.261, 4.69 and 0.261. That bound is deliberately not a budget: it is a cliff detector for the class CPU cannot see at all, a workload getting slower in wall while its CPU cost holds flat, which is what blocking on I/O, a network call or a lock wait looks like. The report prints no elapsed time at all: a verdict and no number.

PROVENANCE. measured_commit is 94e8a78, the remote head those five dispatches resolved --ref issue-81-82 against. `population` is the digest of the 780 node ids THAT TREE COLLECTED, computed by running collect_node_ids over a checkout of it — the same derivation the control performs — rather than copied from anywhere. Entries, wall and population therefore all describe one head, which is what discharges N1.

HOW TO RE-DERIVE. Run the job at least four or five times on the cell that will read it, and take each entry's min and max ACROSS dispatches AND across windows rather than within one — a single quiet window is not a measurement of the cell, it is a measurement of a quiet afternoon. Keep every window's figures: the widest one seen for an entry governs. Re-derive, never carry, and never shrink because the latest runs were kind.
